The '''2017–18 Butler Bulldogs men's basketball team''' represented [[Butler University]] in the [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. They were coached by [[LaVall Jordan]], in his first year as head coach of his alma mater. The Bulldogs played their home games at [[Hinkle Fieldhouse]] in [[Indianapolis|Indianapolis, Indiana]] as members of the [[Big East Conference]]. They finished the season 21–14, 9–9 in [[2017–18 Big East Conference men's basketball season|Big East play]] to finish a tie for sixth place. As the No. 6 seed in the [[2018 Big East men's basketball tournament|Big East tournament]], they defeated [[2017–18 Seton Hall Pirates men's basketball team|Seton Hall]] before losing to [[2017–18 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team|Villanova]] in the semifinals. They received an at-large bid to the [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as the No. 10 seed in the Midwest region. There they defeated [[2017–18 Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball team|Arkansas]] in the first round before losing to [[2017–18 Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball team|Purdue]] in the second round.

== Previous season ==
The [[2016–17 Butler Bulldogs men's basketball team|Bulldogs]] finished the [[2016–17 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2016–17 season]] 25–9, 12–6 in [[2016–17 Big East Conference men's basketball season|Big East play]] to finish in second place. They lost to [[2016–17 Xavier Musketeers men's basketball team|Xavier]] in the quarterfinals of the [[2017 Big East men's basketball tournament|Big East tournament]]. The team received an at-large bid to the [[2017 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as a No. 4 seed in the South Region. They defeated No. 13 [[2016–17 Winthrop Eagles men's basketball team|Winthrop]] and No. 12 [[2016–17 Middle Tennessee Blue Raiders men's basketball team|Middle Tennessee]] to advance to the Sweet 16. In the Sweet 16, they lost to eventual National Champion [[2016–17 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]].

On June 9, 2017, head coach [[Chris Holtmann]] left the school to become the head coach at [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2017/06/09/chris-holtmann-to-be-named-new-ohio-state-basketball-coach/102664630/|title=Butler's Chris Holtmann hired as Ohio State coach|work=USA TODAY|access-date=2017-06-09|language=en}}</ref> On June 12, the school hired [[Milwaukee Panthers men's basketball|Milwaukee]] head coach and Butler alum LaVall Jordan as head coach.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/college/butler/2017/06/12/butler-targeting-lavall-jordan-next-basketball-coach/390953001/|title=Butler stays in the family: New coach is LaVall Jordan|work=Indianapolis Star|access-date=2017-06-13|language=en}}</ref>

===2017 recruiting class===
Butler originally signed five recruits in its 2017 class which was hailed as the best recruiting class in Butler history.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/college/butler/2016/11/09/signing-day-butlers-highest-ranked-recruiting-class-features-versatility/93538184/|title=Signing Day: Butler's highest-ranked recruiting class features versatility|website=Indianapolis Star|access-date=2017-07-10}}</ref> Following Chris Holtmann's departure, however, top-rated recruited [[Kyle Young]] was released from his letter of intent and followed Holtmann to Ohio State.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/college/butler/2017/06/19/butlers-top-recruit-flips-ohio-state-i-want-part-building-something-special-my-home-state/410729001/|title=Butler's top recruit flips to Ohio State: 'I want to be part of building something special in my home state.'|website=Indianapolis Star|access-date=2017-07-10}}</ref> On October 8, 2017, Cooper Neese announced he would be transferring to [[Indiana State Sycamores men's basketball|Indiana State]] before the season began.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/college/butler/2017/10/08/ini-1008-cooper-neese-transfer-butler/744029001/|title=Cooper Neese to transfer from Butler before freshman season even starts|website=Indianapolis Star|access-date=2017-10-08}}</ref>

== Preseason ==
